title: Customer Health Storyline — QBR Decks (Standard + Enterprise) & Renewal Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working draft outlines two parallel QBR deck variants (Standard and Enterprise) centered on a customer-health storytelling approach plus an embedded renewal tracker and a step-by-step playbook for CSMs. Goal: make our QBRs make the renewal conversation natural, data-driven, and action-oriented while surfacing risk earlier.

Audience:
- CSMs running renewal and growth QBRs
- Customer Success Managers partnering with AE/AM on renewals
- Rev Ops & CS leadership for operationalizing tracker fields

High-level approach / thesis:
- Move away from templated slides that only show topline metrics. Instead: build a 6‑part narrative arc that connects adoption signals, value delivered, open risks, win plans, usage patterns, and commercial next steps.
- Embed a single-page renewal tracker that is updated weekly and summarized in the QBR.

Slide-by-slide outline (Standard deck — 12 slides, 20 minute meeting):
1) Cover + meeting objectives (2 bullets: review health, agree next steps)
2) One-line account health snapshot (traffic light + 1-sentence thesis)
3) Value delivered this quarter (top 3 wins, customer-quoted outcomes)
4) Usage & feature adoption highlights (charts: DAU/WAU, top features used)
5) Customer sentiment + support heatmap (NPS trend, top 3 support ticket themes)
6) Risks and blockers (prioritized, with owner and ETA)
7) Opportunities & expansion hypotheses (specific feature+use-case asks)
8) Renewal status snapshot (renewal date, ACV, indicated likelihood) — summary from tracker
9) Recommended next steps & timeline (CSM + customer commitments)
10) Ask / decision items (what we need from executive sponsor)
11) Appendix: adoption artifacts and exec quotes
12) Action item slide (owners, dates)

Slide-by-slide outline (Enterprise deck — 18 slides, 45 minute meeting):
- Expand Standard with: deeper exec story, risk remediation plan, TCO/cost-savings modeling, compliance/audit readiness slide, technical milestones for private deployments, case studies of similar customers, rollout plan for next 12 months with resourcing ask.
- Add a one-page "Fallback & Contingency" showing service-level routing and model variants we recommend if performance issues arise.

Sentiment-driven elements (differentiator):
- Pull NPS, CSAT, support ticket sentiment, and product usage comments into a single 1-slide sentiment narrative. Include 1–2 verbatim customer quotes (positive and constructive) to humanize the data.
- Use simple traffic-light rules to turn sentiment+usage deltas into risk bands.

Renewal tracker (single-page canonical view; maintain weekly):
Required columns (suggested):
- Customer Name (string)
- Renewal Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- ARR/ACV (numeric shown as $)
- Current Likelihood (Very High/High/Medium/Low)
- Primary Risk (short text)
- Mitigation Owner (name)
- Next Contact (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Commitment (what customer has agreed to e.g., PO, verbal, RFP)
- Notes (free text)
Operational notes: keep this sheet as source-of-truth and surface top 5 at each QBR. Rev Ops should export a weekly snapshot to the CSM team Slack channel.

Playbook (pre/during/post QBR):
Pre-QBR (7–10 days out):
- Run renewal-tracker extract, update risk fields.
- Reach out to exec sponsor to confirm agenda and objective.
- Pull 1 customer quote and 2 usage examples for the deck.
- Run quick health-check call with technical lead if there are open engineering items.

During QBR:
- Start with thesis and 1-sentence health summary.
- Always surface the top 3 risks early, then show remediation plan.
- End with explicit asks: signatures, PO timeline, or pilot commitments.

Post-QBR (24–72 hours):
- Send follow-up email with slides + updated renewal tracker row.
- Create JIRA/Linear ticket for any product/eng actions, link to customer thread.
- Update internal deal room: change likelihood per outcomes and flag for AE handoff if needed.

Speaker notes / scripts (sample lines for CSM):
- Open: "In the last 90 days we saw X% adoption growth and two concrete outcomes: A and B — this is why we think the product is delivering value."
- Risk callout: "We flagged three items that could impact renewal; we've assigned owners and timelines and expect resolution ahead of the renewal window."
- Close: "To keep this momentum we recommend the three next steps on slide 9. Do you have any constraints on timing for the PO?"

Operational checklist for slide build (CSM):
- Pull last 90-day usage report (platform analytics).
- Run support heatmap (top 5 ticket themes).
- Confirm quote and current ARR with AE/finance.
- Validate exec sponsor attendance.

Metrics & visualizations guidance:
- Use sparklines for trend data, not raw tables.
- Prefer % delta vs prior quarter for adoption metrics.
- For Enterprise: include small TCO calc (savings per 1k calls after batching/caching).

Open questions / decisions needed (for leadership):
- Should we add a standard one-line scoring algorithm (health score = usage*sentiment - unresolved_tickets_weight)? Do we want a baked-in formula or leave as CSM judgment?
- Can Rev Ops surface contract start/end and ARR automatically into the tracker? (JIRA-CS-1422)

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Rev Ops to prototype the renewal tracker export (Diego) — ETA 2025-12-01
- Enable a slide template in Drive with prefilled charts (Maya) — ETA 2025-12-15
- Pilot with 6 mid-market accounts for January QBRs (Oliver) — target complete 2026-01-31

Notes to self / rough ideas to iterate:
- Consider a one-pager "value calculator" we can run live in meeting for enterprise finance teams.
- Experiment with embedding short customer-recorded clip (30s) as proof point for exec-level QBRs.

Unresolved:
- Final nomenclature for likelihood buckets (Verbal vs Committed vs PO).
- Whether to expose internal risk scoring to customers in the deck (probably not).

Attachments & templates to add to this doc:
- Standard deck PPTX template (to create)
